The MBR combines the secondary biological treatment and immersed membrane filtration processes.
Disinfection is achieved in an open channel UV disinfection system with sufficient low pressure/high output lamps to disinfect a peak daily flow of 4.0 mgd.
return activated sludge pumping from the MBR back to the aeration basins.

Waste activated sludge pumping removes excessive biomass from the system, followed by a proprietary sludge digestion process, dewatering via centrifuge, and disposal to a Class III solid waste landfill.
The Facility includes a 5 million gallon aerated influent equalization basin
and a 3.35 million gallon equalization basin, which provides equalization storage capacity for extended wet weather flows and plant return flows.
The Facility has two recycled water storage ponds, 25 million gallon and 15 million gallon capacity, with synthetic liners to provide storage for the disinfected tertiary treated recycled water

Filtered and UV disinfected wastewater flows by gravity to the 25 million gallon recycled water storage pond, 15 million gallon recycled water storage pond, or Basalt Pond.
The MBR filtrate pumps discharge directly to the UV basin.
All solids transferred from the biological process to the interchange reactors are first passed through a 250 micron rotary drum screen to remove inert non-biodegradable material,
The Permittee uses a proprietary solids removal and digestion process that combines aerobic and anaerobic processes.
decanted clear liquid from the interchange reactors is returned to the biological process, and the volume decanted is replaced with solids from the biological process.
digested solids are pumped from the interchange reactor tanks, dosed with polymer for thickening, and then dewatered in a centrifuge and conveyed to a dumpster.

All solids are then transported for disposal at Redwood Landfill in Marin County or Hay Road Landfill in Solano County.
The Permittee has the ability to divert inadequately treated wastewater from downstream of the UV disinfection system and return it to the headworks for re-treatment.
